name: Scam compounds and end-to-end scam-proceeds flows
description: Industrialised online-fraud operations (investment, romance and impersonation scams, including pig-butchering) run from compound-style premises, often staffed by people recruited under false pretences and held in forced labour. The financial footprint spans victim payments, recruited receiving accounts, consolidation, crypto conversion and cash-out, plus corporate fronts and infrastructure spending that sustain the operation. Defensive framing: this entry lists observable financial signals for institutions, not operating methods. See FR-ROM (victim journey) and HT-FORCEDLAB (labour exploitation) for context only.

sources.text: FATF, INTERPOL and Egmont Group, Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-enabled Fraud (2023)
FinCEN, Alert on Prevalent Virtual Currency Investment Scam Commonly Known as Pig Butchering (2023)
UNODC, Transnational Organized Crime and the Convergence of Cyber-Enabled Fraud, Underground Banking and Technological Innovation in Southeast Asia (2024)

exposure.rationale: Victims approached via social and messaging platforms; mule accounts collect and consolidate, then crypto off-ramps or wires abroad.

indicators.name: Accounts used as pass-through for overseas scam operations
indicators.canon: Accounts used as pass-through for overseas scam operations
indicators.desc: recruited accounts receive victim funds and convert quickly to stablecoins or wire abroad.
indicators.ctx: Recruited or complicit account holders receive victim funds and quickly convert to stablecoins or wire abroad, the core mule step in the compound payment chain.
indicators.fp: May have innocent explanations; assess in context of customer profile and other indicators.

indicators.name: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims
indicators.canon: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims
indicators.desc: A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
indicators.ctx: A low-activity account receives payments from several apparent investment or romance scam victims, sometimes with narratives referencing a "platform" or "trading".
indicators.fp: Legitimate sales, crowdfunding or refunds can look similar; check payment references and account history.

indicators.name: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
indicators.canon: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
indicators.desc: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.
indicators.ctx: New or reactivated receiving accounts collect payments from unrelated individuals, matching the collection tier that feeds a compound's consolidation accounts.
indicators.fp: Fundraising, club accounts or small traders with genuine many-to-one inflows.

indicators.name: Funds routed to multiple small accounts then consolidated
indicators.canon: Funds routed to multiple small accounts then consolidated
indicators.desc: Mule-side: scam proceeds are split across many personal and corporate accounts before consolidation and cash-out.
indicators.ctx: Victim payments are split across many personal and corporate accounts then consolidated to a small number of accounts or exchange deposits.
indicators.fp: Payroll or marketplace payouts with similar structure.

indicators.name: Destination wallet linked to scam or fraud clusters
indicators.canon: Destination wallet linked to scam or fraud clusters
indicators.desc: Receiving address is attributed to investment, romance or impersonation scams.
indicators.ctx: Victim deposits or onward transfers reach wallet addresses attributed by analytics providers to fake investment platforms or scam clusters.

indicators.name: Shared devices, IP addresses or contact details across accounts
indicators.canon: Shared devices, IP addresses or contact details across accounts
indicators.desc: Multiple unrelated accounts share devices, phone numbers, email or addresses.
indicators.ctx: Dozens of apparently unrelated receiving or onboarding accounts share devices, IP ranges, phone numbers or documents, indicating one operating group behind many accounts.
indicators.fp: Households and shared workplaces share details.

indicators.name: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.canon: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.desc: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.
indicators.ctx: Scam proceeds leave rapidly to offshore accounts or are converted to virtual assets within hours of credit, the cash-out end of the chain.
indicators.fp: Genuine international payments or planned crypto purchases by established customers.

indicators.name: Funds sent to unlicensed or weakly regulated exchanges
indicators.canon: Funds sent to unlicensed or weakly regulated exchanges
indicators.desc: Withdrawals or flows go to exchanges or VASPs that lack licensing or effective AML and sanctions controls.
indicators.ctx: Consolidated proceeds are sent to exchanges, OTC desks or platforms with weak licensing or AML controls, enabling off-ramp into fiat or further layering.
indicators.fp: Some legitimate smaller platforms are not yet registered or are licensed in other regimes.

indicators.name: Operating-company profile with scam-infrastructure spending and no business footprint
indicators.canon: Operating-company profile with scam-infrastructure spending and no business footprint
indicators.desc: A corporate customer in recruitment, customer-service outsourcing, gaming, crypto or consultancy, often with remote principals, shows spending on bulk telecoms, servers, hosting, domains, devices and accommodation but little revenue, payroll or customer activity consistent with its stated business.
indicators.ctx: Front or service companies that fund the physical and technical operation of a compound appear as customers whose spending profile fits infrastructure rather than their declared business.
indicators.fp: Legitimate offshore call centres, start-ups, IT outsourcers and marketing firms also spend heavily on infrastructure and may have thin early-stage revenue and remote ownership.

indicators.name: Payments by relatives for release or "fees" for a person held abroad
indicators.canon: Payments by relatives for release or "fees" for a person held abroad
indicators.desc: Customers, often family members, send urgent payments abroad described as fees, fines or bail to secure the release of a relative who travelled for work, sometimes to many different recipient accounts or wallets.
indicators.ctx: Families of people held in forced labour at a compound may pay demanded sums; the customer can be a victim of coercion and needs a referral path rather than an exit.
indicators.fp: Genuine emergency payments for relatives in legal or medical difficulty abroad, or legitimate bail and consular costs, can look similar.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
